newsitem.title: SPAIN: BASKETBALL-ITALY AND GREECE THROUGH, CROATIA STUMBLE.
newsitem.headline: BASKETBALL-ITALY AND GREECE THROUGH, CROATIA STUMBLE.

text.p: Italy and Greece each booked places in the quarter-finals of the European basketball championship on Sunday with hard fought wins over Spain and Lithuania respectively.
Despite the results, both Spain and Lithuania will almost certainly also go through, as will Yugoslavia, who beat Germany.
But heavily-tipped Croatia look likely to miss the cut after losing by one point to Poland, their third consecutive defeat.
Results from the first phase games are also used to determine second phase group classifications.
Italy, Spain, Greece and Lithuania all won their opening three games.

Spain looked set to continue their unbeaten run after opening a 36-25 lead at halftime. The Italians fought back in the second term, and after seeing Alfonso Reyes foul out, the home side gave up a crucial loss of possession with 50 seconds on the clock, and Italy took the game 63-60.
In one of the most exciting games so far Greece kept Lithuanian forward Arturas Karnisovas down to just nine points and came out on top 73-66.

Croatia went in at the break with a 12-point lead over Poland, before succumbing 77-76. Croatia will have to win both their remaining games, and see other results go their way to stay in the competition.
Yugoslavia's comfortable 88-73 win over Germany left the 1993 champions in danger of elimination, having lost three out of four games.
In other matches Turkey trailed 26-35 at halftime but came out strongly after the break to outscore a nervous Israeli side 17-1, and went on to take the game 81-71.
France were left close to elimination after losing 93-80 to Russia.
